scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is native to Megara Attikis, Greece.
It is centered around a song about a boat named Loulouvikos that took the young men of the village away, serving as a cultural memory of maritime departure.
on_screen: Map: Greece · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is a playful carnival dance.
While the lyrics are about the sadness of departure, the dance itself is a display of strength and humor, particularly during the competitive pushing at the end.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: It begins with a 'Sta Tria' step pattern in a circle.
During the chorus, dancers perform up to 20 squats while continuing to move in the circle.
It often ends with dancers pushing each other to see who falls.
Watch for Loulouvikos Squats, The Fall.

Formation: Starts in a circle; ends with dancers breaking off into open space for pushing.
